2026-11-07.headline: NDES guidance adds SID certificate request settings and validation safeguards
2026-11-07.overview: A new AD CS article explains how to configure NDES to accept SID information in certificate requests through registry settings for SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Enable the settings only when a trusted component validates the SID. Incorrect validation could enable impersonation or elevation of privilege; apply the changes by resetting IIS or restarting NDES.

keyChanges.title: New AD CS guidance covers SID-enabled NDES requests
keyChanges.detail: The article documents registry configuration for accepting SID information in certificate requests, including SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats. It advises that a trusted component validate the SID before enabling these settings and specifies resetting IIS or restarting NDES to apply changes.

2026-11-11.headline: SID-bearing certificate requests: NDES guidance explains SAN, extension, and custom policy-module exception
2026-11-11.overview: The 11 November batch was largely documentation maintenance, with the most substantive update in AD CS. NDES guidance now covers certificate requests carrying SID information in the SAN or a separate SID extension, including the custom policy module exception. Other meaningful edits refresh VM conversion links for VDDK 8.0.3 and Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting, while Active Directory and AD FS received narrower reference and wording updates.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Review the NDES guidance when designing or troubleshooting certificate enrollment involving SID data. For VM conversion, use the updated Broadcom Support link to obtain VDDK 8.0.3; the required version and extraction path are unchanged. The OWASP and CBT changes direct administrators to updated external resources, and no action is indicated for the AD FS revision.

keyChanges.title: NDES guidance details SID data in SANs and separate certificate extensions
keyChanges.detail: The AD CS article now describes NDES behavior for requests containing SID information in the SAN or in a separate SID extension, including the exception for custom policy modules. Administrators working on affected enrollment scenarios should consult this guidance during design or troubleshooting.

keyChanges.title: VM conversion guidance links directly to Broadcom for VDDK 8.0.3
keyChanges.detail: The migration procedure now points to Broadcom Support for downloading VMware VDDK 8.0.3. The required version and extraction path remain unchanged, so the practical action is to use the updated download link.

keyChanges.title: Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting now uses a new Broadcom guide URL
keyChanges.detail: The VM conversion troubleshooting article now links to a new Broadcom VDDK Programming Guide URL for Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting. Administrators following the article will be directed to that updated resource.

keyChanges.title: Active Directory security guidance now links to OWASP’s 2025 Top 10
keyChanges.detail: The Avenues To Compromise article replaces its former OWASP index link with the OWASP 2025 Top 10 page, directing readers to current vulnerability and countermeasure information. No configuration change is required.

keyChanges.title: AD FS smart-lockout guidance revises proxy request wording and metadata
keyChanges.detail: The AD FS extranet smart lockout article received updated DevRel metadata links and a minor revision describing ESL requests through Web Application Proxy or an MS-ADFSPIP-compatible third-party proxy. No administrator action is indicated.

2026-11-12.headline: AD FS FAQ ties unknown domain identifiers to controller discovery and CLDAP safeguards
2026-11-12.overview: An updated AD FS troubleshooting FAQ explains that unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can trigger domain controller discovery, including DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout on Windows Server 2019 and later, along with restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: AD FS administrators should review these security recommendations and verify authentication, including cross-forest authentication, after applying firewall restrictions.

keyChanges.title: AD FS guidance details domain-controller discovery triggered by unknown identifiers
keyChanges.detail: The FAQ says unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can initiate domain controller discovery through DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout for Windows Server 2019 and later and restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.

2026-11-13.headline: RD Web Access XSLT customizations face Chromium M158 cutoff November 17, 2026
2026-11-13.overview: New Remote Desktop guidance covers assessing, migrating, validating, and troubleshooting RD Web Access customizations that rely on browser-native XSLT. Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT beginning November 17, 2026.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Administrators with affected customizations should migrate before the cutoff. They should leave the updated .aspx pages unchanged, configure a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath, and test sign-in, resource access, and password changes.

keyChanges.title: Migration path added for RD Web Access XSLT customizations
keyChanges.detail: The guidance explains how to assess, migrate, validate, and troubleshoot customizations using browser-native XSLT. It directs administrators to keep the updated .aspx pages unchanged and configure a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath before Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT on November 17, 2026.

2026-11-14.headline: DNS Server adds Event 506 and relocates debug logs outside its default directory
2026-11-14.overview: The period’s most consequential guidance concerns DNS logging and Windows Admin Center compatibility. Applicable 2026 cumulative updates are documented as logging DNS Event ID 506 and relocating existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`; changing `LogFilePath` now requires local Administrators membership. Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 is documented as moving to .NET 10, with Azure Connected Machine Agent 1.65 or earlier unable to upgrade to that version or later. Failover Cluster Manager guidance also tightens the campus-cluster procedure around KB5072033, the fault-domain property, and storage-pool version.
2026-11-14.adminImpact: Audit DNS debug-log locations and operator permissions before applying applicable 2026 cumulative updates. Update Azure Connected Machine Agent versions 1.65 or earlier before upgrading Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 or later. For campus clusters, apply KB5072033 to every participating server, use `FaultDomainAwarenessDefault`, and verify storage pool version 29 or later.

keyChanges.title: DNS guidance documents new logging and permission behavior
keyChanges.detail: Starting with applicable 2026 cumulative updates, DNS Server logs Event ID 506 and relocates existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`. Changing `LogFilePath` requires membership in local Administrators; DnsAdmins membership alone is denied.

keyChanges.title: Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 moves to .NET 10
keyChanges.detail: The 1.3.0.0 release upgrades Windows Admin Center to .NET 10. Azure Connected Machine Agent version 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to this Windows Admin Center version or later versions.

keyChanges.title: Arc agent guidance preserves connection and upgrade boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The Arc hybrid-machine guidance states that agent versions 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to Windows Admin Center 1.0.0.0 or later. It also records that Arc agent versions 1.35 and 1.36 break Windows Admin Center connections, while version 1.37 and later fix that issue.

keyChanges.title: Campus-cluster instructions revise the fault-domain and storage prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Failover Cluster Manager procedure now scopes KB5072033 to every server joining the cluster, replaces `FaultDomainAwareness` checks with `FaultDomainAwarenessDefault`, and clarifies the requirement for storage pool version 29 or later.

2026-11-02.headline: New NDES guidance covers SID certificate requests through two registry formats
2026-11-02.overview: The week brought one new AD CS procedure: configuring Network Device Enrollment Service (NDES) to accept SID information in certificate requests through SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Enable the settings only when a trusted component validates the SID, because incorrect validation could enable impersonation or elevation of privilege. Apply the configuration by resetting IIS or restarting NDES.

keyChanges.title: NDES SID request configuration
keyChanges.detail: The new AD CS article explains how to use registry settings for the SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats when configuring NDES to accept SID information in certificate requests. It also specifies the validation condition and requires an IIS reset or NDES restart after applying the changes.

2026-11-09.headline: Chromium’s XSLT cutoff sets a November 17 RD Web Access migration deadline
2026-11-09.overview: The week’s most immediate administrator deadline is Chromium M158 disabling browser-native XSLT on November 17, 2026, affecting customized RD Web Access pages. Windows Server also introduced an LDAP authentication requirement for Kerberos service-ticket and LDAP SPN matching, while applicable 2026-11 cumulative updates alter DNS debug-log handling. Windows Server 2016 extended support ends January 13, 2027, and Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 adds an Azure Connected Machine Agent compatibility gate. Additional AD FS guidance covers Extranet Smart Lockout and outbound CLDAP restrictions; most remaining edits were documentation and procedure maintenance.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Administrators with affected RD Web Access customizations should migrate before November 17 and test sign-in, resource access, and password changes. For NetApp SMB environments using LDAP authentication, verify that Kerberos service tickets match the LDAP SPN registered on the target domain controller. After applicable 2026-11 updates, review DNS debug-log locations and use a local Administrators account for LogFilePath changes; DnsAdmins membership alone is insufficient. Include the January 13, 2027, Windows Server 2016 support deadline in upgrade planning, and update Azure Connected Machine Agent version 1.65 or earlier before upgrading Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 or later.

keyChanges.title: RD Web Access customizations need migration before Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT
keyChanges.detail: New guidance states that Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT beginning November 17, 2026. Affected deployments should leave the updated .aspx pages unchanged, configure a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath, and validate sign-in, resource display, and password-change workflows.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server LDAP authentication now requires Kerberos tickets to match the target LDAP SPN
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s security notice says the October 13, 2026, Windows security updates introduced additional LDAP authentication requirements for domain controllers. Kerberos service tickets used for LDAP authentication must match the LDAP service principal name registered on the target domain controller, a requirement called out for preventing NetApp SMB share issues.

keyChanges.title: DNS Server changes debug-log placement and restricts LogFilePath changes
keyChanges.detail: With applicable 2026-11 cumulative updates, DNS Server logs Event ID 506 and relocates existing debug logs configured outside C:\Windows\System32\dns\log. Changing LogFilePath requires local Administrators membership; DnsAdmins membership alone is denied.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server 2016 extended support ends January 13, 2027
keyChanges.detail: All Windows Server 2016 editions reach the end of extended support on January 13, 2027. The January 2027 Windows security update will be the last update provided during extended support.

keyChanges.title: Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 blocks upgrades from older Arc agents
keyChanges.detail: Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 upgrades to .NET 10, and Azure Connected Machine Agent version 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to this or later Windows Admin Center versions. The documented upgrade path therefore requires updating the agent first.

2026-11.headline: RD Web Access customizations face a November 17 Chromium XSLT cutoff
2026-11.overview: An imminent Chromium compatibility break dominates November: M158 disables browser-native XSLT on November 17, 2026, putting affected RD Web Access customizations on a migration deadline. Windows Server also tightened LDAP authentication after the October 13 security updates, changed DNS debug-log handling with applicable November cumulative updates, and set a January 13, 2027 support endpoint for every Windows Server 2016 edition. AD CS added focused NDES guidance for SID-bearing certificate requests.
2026-11.adminImpact: Administrators with customized RD Web Access pages should migrate and test sign-in, resource access, and password changes before November 17. For LDAP-authenticated integrations, especially NetApp SMB scenarios, verify that Kerberos service tickets match the LDAP SPN on the target domain controller. Review DNS debug-log paths and account permissions after applicable November cumulative updates. Treat January 13, 2027, as the final Windows Server 2016 extended-support date, and enable NDES SID settings only when a trusted component validates the SID; reset IIS or restart NDES after applying them.

keyChanges.title: Chromium M158 sets a November 17 cutoff for browser-native XSLT in RD Web Access
keyChanges.detail: Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT beginning November 17, 2026. Affected customizations should use a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath, while the updated .aspx pages remain unchanged; administrators should then test sign-in, resource access, and password changes.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server LDAP authentication now requires the target domain controller’s LDAP SPN to match
keyChanges.detail: The October 13, 2026, Windows security updates introduced additional LDAP authentication requirements: Kerberos service tickets used for LDAP authentication must match the LDAP service principal name (SPN) registered on the target domain controller. The Message Center notice specifically calls out NetApp SMB shares.

keyChanges.title: November DNS updates change debug-log handling and restrict LogFilePath changes
keyChanges.detail: Starting with applicable 2026-11 cumulative updates, DNS Server logs Event ID 506 and relocates existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`. Changing `LogFilePath` requires membership in the local Administrators group; DnsAdmins membership alone is denied.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server 2016 extended support ends January 13, 2027
keyChanges.detail: All Windows Server 2016 editions reach the end of extended support on January 13, 2027. The January 2027 Windows security update will be the last update provided during extended support.

keyChanges.title: New AD CS guidance documents NDES configuration for SID certificate requests
keyChanges.detail: The new procedure explains how to configure NDES to accept SID information in certificate requests through registry settings for SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats. The settings should be enabled only when a trusted component validates the SID, because incorrect validation could enable impersonation or elevation of privilege; applying them requires resetting IIS or restarting NDES.
